title: Setting the rate: at or below income growth
objectives: Apply the rule of thumb for the step-up rate.
Explain what happens when the step-up outruns income.
body_md:
The rate is the easiest part of the conversation, once the four checks are done.

## The rule of thumb

Set the step-up at or below the client's expected income growth. If income grows 8–10% a year, a 5–10% step-up is usually comfortable.

## Why not higher

A step-up faster than income growth squeezes the budget within a few years. By year three the instalment is a visibly larger share of pay, and the client either cancels it or starts missing debits.

## How to frame it

"What share of your raise could go to savings?" If the answer is a third to a half, the step-up rate is simply that share of the expected raise. The client sees the money as coming out of the raise, not out of today's spending.

## When income is uncertain

Pick the lower end, or use a fixed amount the client is sure about. The rate can be raised at the next review; it cannot be un-cancelled.
example: Income expected to grow 8% a year: a 5–8% step-up is comfortable and leaves room for the EMI the client expects next year. A 15% step-up would be cancelled by year three.
say: Let's set the step-up at or below what your income is likely to grow by.
If your raise is 10%, sending half of it to the SIP is a 5% step-up.
never: Let's do 20% so you catch up faster.
The rate doesn't matter; the fund's return does.

talk_track.text: The rule of thumb: step up at or below the client's expected income growth. If income grows eight to ten percent a year, a five to ten percent step-up is usually comfortable. A step-up faster than income growth will squeeze the budget within a few years.

check.q: How much of each raise should a comfortable step-up roughly reflect?
check.why: If a third to a half of each raise is free to save, that share of the expected raise sets a comfortable step-up.

check.q: Income is expected to grow 8–10% a year. What step-up fits?
check.why: At or below income growth: 5–10% is usually comfortable.

check.q: What happens when a step-up outruns income growth?
o: The client saves more, so it always works
The instalment becomes a visibly larger share of pay and gets cancelled or missed
check.why: Unsustainable step-ups are cancelled or missed, which costs more than never stepping up.
